single_ablation.conclusion: The opposite common factor was not the bottleneck. The V53 stop-outs did not become completed old-boundary failures within the allowed causal horizon, even when the common-turn requirement was removed.

failure_classification.dominant_failure: V53 losses were incorrectly generalized as failed auctions. Their narrow structural stops were traversed, but the accepted external boundary itself was not lost. Directional state and entry/stop timing must be separated.

valid_components_preserved: do not reverse immediately against an accepted auction
require an explicit old-boundary failure before failed-auction reversal
opposite common-factor and index-proxy confirmation remains a valid reversal contract
next_hypothesis: The accepted-auction direction may remain valid, but the first FVG hold is not a completed entry state. Wait for a multi-bar boundary/FVG negotiation, then enter only when the common factor resolves the entire prior negotiation range in the accepted direction; invalidate beyond the full negotiation extreme.
